coverage: 20 sources reached, 13 substantive, 46 claims, every non-empty quotation re-checked against the fetched text before writing. ROSTER: (1) JFA 20.2 (2009) — Crossref does not index the journal (api.crossref.org/journals/0897-0521 = 404), so the issue was enumerated from OpenAlex source S2764679916, which shows nine articles and gives no DOI for any of them; the only landing pages OpenAlex carries are on the defunct Questia. Wolfe, "Guy Gavriel Kay: An Introduction" (p. 238) FETCHED as an opening-paragraph excerpt from a 2015 Wayback id_ capture of the Questia page — the previous round recorded it BLOCKED because the availability API was queried without the www. prefix, which is what makes the snapshot resolve. Kay's own "The Fiction of Privacy: Fantasy and the Past" (pp. 240-47), which the angle did not name, FETCHED the same way as an excerpt, and its source text — the 4 November 2000 Convocation Hall address "Reflections on an Ethical Society" — FETCHED IN FULL from Kay's authorized site, whose end-note establishes the JFA article as its revision. JFA 13.2 NOT REACHED: the OpenAlex daily budget was exhausted mid-sweep and no other index enumerates the journal. (2) Toswell 2025 BLOCKED, and the angle's premise CORRECTED — it is not a book-length study of Kay but M. J. Toswell, Medievalism in English Canadian Identity and Literature (Arc Humanities/Amsterdam UP, 2025), in which Kay is ch. 3, "Guy Gavriel Kay: Historical Fantasy", pp. 89-124 (10.1515/9781802703696-006; JSTOR 10.2307/jj.32561711.8). No abstract in Crossref or OpenAlex, De Gruyter Brill returns HTTP 202 with an empty body, JSTOR serves a 3,038-byte bot shell, the book is in neither OAPEN nor DOAB, and the Google Books API quota was exhausted. Toswell's earlier articles on The Last Light of the Sun: NEGATIVE FINDING — no such article exists in Crossref or OpenAlex; her Kay work is the 2025 chapter and her editorship of the 2020 Boydell volume. (3) Siourbas BLOCKED at the chapter text but LOCATED and CORRECTED: the full title is "More Than Just Survival: The Successful Quest for Voice in Guy Gavriel Kay's Tigana and Randy Bradshaw's The Song Spinner", pp. 73-80 of Worlds of Wonder (U Ottawa Press 2004, 10.1353/book6623); the Project MUSE book record yields the table of contents but no chapter link without a licence, the chapter is in neither Crossref nor OpenAlex nor Erudit nor OAPEN nor RUOR, and Open Library's search-inside finds the title only in bibliographies and indexes. (4) Borowska-Szerszun "Remembering the Romance" FETCHED as a chapter-opening extract — the /core/books/abs/ slug 404s, but the Crossref record's resource.primary URL (/core/product/identifier/9781787448858%23c10/type/book_part) renders; academia.edu and ResearchGate were not needed. "When Gods are Absent from Fantasy" FETCHED IN FULL: the 4.7 MB Bialystok scan is an image-only Konica-Minolta PDF yielding zero extractable text, cracked by pulling its 18 embedded page JPEGs with pypdf and OCRing each with tesseract 5.5.3 (36,724 characters). (5) All five keyword-only sources READ IN FULL — Taylor "The Double-Edged Gift", Doherty, Clements, Labrousse-Marchau, and Medievalists.net (three pages: the substantive 2016 Alvarez interview, plus the 2010 and 2019 pages, which are blurbs around dead or audio-only content). NEGATIVE FINDING on the five: Taylor and Clements are thematic readings of Fionavar that say almost nothing about register or the description of places, so they yield one claim each. ROUTES: 8 substantive by live raw HTML, 3 by Cambridge Core identifier-endpoint extracts, 2 by Wayback id_ captures of the defunct Questia, 1 by OCR of an image-only scan, 1 by an open-access PDF binary plus pdftotext, 1 abstract-only via OpenAlex. EXPANSION added Laszkiewicz's Atlantis 46.1 (2024) article — the only source found in either round that analyses how this kind of fantasy describes a CITY, and it does so as a criticism — plus Drab on Ysabel and two further Borowska-Szerszun pieces. The web-search budget was exhausted before this sweep began and DuckDuckGo and Mojeek both refuse automated queries, so discovery ran on Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Project MUSE, Open Library, the Wayback availability API and bibliography chasing alone; the Internet Archive CDX endpoint was offline throughout. Two consecutive expansion queries (the full Crossref enumeration of Kay-titled scholarship, and the JFA volume walk) surfaced nothing new.
